channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Iran imposes sweeping measures as U.S. economic pressure mounts
item.description: Tehran is rolling back subsidies on bread and gasoline, deepening discontent with the government amid a worsening economic crisis after nearly nine months of war.

item.title: How long Thanksgiving leftovers actually last — and the best way to store them
item.description: Taking a few simple steps to properly pack up and store your leftovers on Thanksgiving can play a big role in how long your food stays safe to eat. Follow these tips from food safety experts and USDA.

item.title: Practicing ‘freudenfreude’ can bring more joy to your life. Here’s how.
item.description: I know what it’s like to long for what others have, our guest columnist writes. But I have learned — and science suggests — that finding satisfaction in others’ joy can make hard things more bearable. Such satisfaction is called freudenfreude.

item.title: Many in suburban Maryland asked to conserve water as storm causes power issues, flight delays and flooding along East Coast
item.description: Two water filtration plants in Maryland joined a half-million people facing power issues as the worst Thanksgiving Day storm on the East Coast in decades barreled across the region. Strong winds and rain are disrupting travel, and there is flooding in many coastal communities.

item.title: Strobe Talbott dies at 80. The journalist and diplomat helped shape Bill Clinton’s foreign policy.
item.description: The reporter’s knowledge of Russia and U.S.-Soviet relations was the foundation of a long, influential career. Mr. Talbott helped lead the Clinton administration’s efforts to quell conflicts in the Balkans, expand the NATO military alliance eastward and manage Clinton’s fraught relations with Russia’s erratic leader, Boris Yeltsin.

item.title: Trump says he wants to work with Democrats on health care. But can they find a compromise?
item.description: Democrats, who will have majorities in the House and Senate next year, are focused on boosting Affordable Care Act subsidies and reversing Republican cuts to Medicaid, which are in opposition to President Donald Trump’s policies. But the two sides might be able to work together to lower drug prices, among other issues.

item.title: How Quentin Tarantino took the whole movie world down the rabbit hole
item.description: Thirty years after “Pulp Fiction,” his once-niche obsessions are simply mainstream culture, Will Leitch writes.

item.title: A man with Alzheimer’s who went missing in Maryland turns up in Philadelphia playing a piano outdoors
item.description: Frank Grow’s daughter said the 78-year-old traveled more than 100 miles in an effort to return to where he grew up in Norristown, Pennsylvania, which is near Philadelphia.

item.title: Top U.S. Forest Service official admits ‘wrong decisions’ and ‘deaths’ will result from wildfire shake-up
item.description: In a private session at an industry conference in San Francisco, Michael Boren, the undersecretary of agriculture for national resources and development, made the statement about the Trump administration’s aggressive timeline to reshape how the nation responds to wildfires.

item.title: Powerful Thanksgiving storm threatens East Coast with floods and damaging winds
item.description: The large storm is expected to progress through the Mid-Atlantic region during the day. Officials are warning of dangerous travel conditions, widespread power outages and hurricane-force gusts.

item.title: Sean Hannity has outlasted Fox News rivals. He’s turning his focus to the GOP’s future.
item.description: After 30 years at the network, the conservative political commentator has weathered scandals and watched rivals come and go. Now, he is preparing to size up the Republicans who hope to succeed the president.

item.title: Judge halts FCC review of ABC licenses, saying it likely violates First Amendment
item.description: ABC and its parent company, Disney, sued the FCC in August, accusing the agency of waging a “retaliatory campaign” because President Donald Trump’s administration disapproves of their programming. The FCC, chaired by Trump appointee Brendan Carr, claimed that its decision to review all of ABC’s licenses was because of a probe into the network’s corporate diversity practices.

item.title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to pressure Nvidia into reappointing Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: The Cold War-era Defense Production Act gives presidents extraordinary power to intervene in the economy. Deploying it to restore Huang had been a popular idea in some Silicon Valley circles.

item.description: America passed a national test of character. That’s worth giving thanks.

item.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed by storm, rescheduled for Saturday
item.description: A major storm is expected to impact the East Coast on Thursday.

item.title: Home sale by Rep. Elise Stefanik’s family was deemed ‘unusual,’ D.C. records show
item.description: A rowhome owned by the New York congresswoman was taken off the market after failing to sell for $1.99 million — and then sold in an off-market transaction for $910,000 more than the original price.

item.title: Here are the Black Friday travel deals actually worth your money in this season of offers
item.description: To winnow the crush of sales to something manageable, consider our top picks for the shopping spree that extends into Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday.

item.title: DHS chief Mullin rebuked by White House insiders, but Trump backs him
item.description: Markwayne Mullin has faced criticism for his shaky public response to recent technology-related outages that grounded planes, shut off corporate email systems and disrupted banking networks. President Donald Trump has said he’s doing a good job.

item.title: Do I really need to brine the turkey? Ask us your Thanksgiving cooking questions.
item.description: In a special pre-Thanksgiving edition, recipes editor Becky Krystal and Food team colleagues answer your cooking questions.

item.title: Trump voters stayed home. Here’s the real lesson.
item.description: Firing up the MAGA base won’t rebuild a coalition that depended on voters who were never MAGA.

item.description: Carolyn Hax readers give advice: Without co-workers, husband has no social life but us. What can we do?

item.title: Army conducts planned detonation of lead-based explosives in Iowa town
item.description: With light winds blowing amid freezing temperatures on Wednesday morning, lead particles from the explosion were projected to drift southwest across acres of farmland and into Missouri. Residents of Middletown, Iowa, had been advised to evacuate, but some chose to remain.

item.title: Trump proposes new tariffs on China, Europe and other trade partners
item.description: The new round of import taxes aimed at countries that prop up domestic industries marks the latest effort to replace tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego García arrives in Spain, ending deportation battle with U.S.
item.description: Kilmar Abrego García has arrived in Spain after departing the United States on his own, ending a 20-month legal saga over the fate of a Salvadoran migrant whose case became a symbol of the Trump administration’s aggressive deportation campaign.

item.title: Five things therapists wish you would stop saying to your adult children
item.description: Even when you mean well, these common phrases can shut down a conversation and make it harder to feel close. Here’s what to say instead.

item.title: Signs of danger at Iowa ammunition plant emerged months before Army says it knew, emails show
item.description: Contractors at the facility in Middletown, Iowa, where the government plans to detonate several tons of degrading lead explosives on Wednesday, sought to neutralize the hazardous material nearly six months before the Army says it became aware the munitions posed a risk, documents reviewed by The Washington Post show. Operators’ request to a Georgia-based explosives disposal company on Sept. 24, 2025, asked for a plan to “neutralize and dispose” of 68 drums of lead azide at the plant.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego García will leave U.S. voluntarily to avoid deportation, ending 20-month legal saga
item.description: The Salvadoran migrant living in Maryland was illegally deported to his home country, then brought back to the U.S. and threatened with deportation to African countries.

item.title: My mom had a secret ingredient. I discovered it making stuffed artichokes.
item.description: For Thanksgiving, I will serve this dish filled with memories and love.

item.title: House Democrat vows to investigate Trump’s efforts to reshape Smithsonian after photos of apparent overhaul plan surfaced
item.description: Rep. Chellie Pingree of Maine and the Smithsonian’s outgoing secretary, Lonnie G. Bunch III, defended the institution’s independence a day after news broke of purported plans that include firing more than a dozen employees.

item.title: Trump awards the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani, a longtime friend and former personal lawyer
item.description: Giuliani, a former mayor of New York, became the face of President Donald Trump’s unsuccessful efforts to overturn the results of his 2020 reelection loss. It’s uncommon, although not unprecedented, for a president to give the award to a prominent political ally.

item.title: Democrat flips a Tennessee House district, AP reports, adding to the record majority her party will have in January
item.description: Victoria Broderick has won the U.S. House seat in Tennessee’s 4th Congressional District, according to the Associated Press, giving Democrats 259 seats in the lower chamber — a modern record.

item.title: Army says it must detonate lead azide to avoid a ‘worst-case scenario’ and urges Iowa town’s vulnerable residents to evacuate
item.description: The controlled detonation of the highly sensitive explosive compound set for Wednesday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown is needed, federal officials said, because the lead azide has become increasingly unstable and is at risk to explode on its own.

item.title: Pope Francis’s private diary reveals inner torment, visions of Devil
item.description: In an exclusive interview, the cardinal who curated Francis’s notes said they were full of deeply personal experiences and fears, including a glimpse of “the entrance to hell.”

item.description: New research shows vaccine recommendation changes could leave millions more Americans vulnerable.

item.title: Court clears way for Army plan to detonate hazardous chemicals in Iowa, after Trump moved to delay it
item.description: The ruling follows a tumultuous week of protests, lawsuits and delays, including a Monday missive from President Donald Trump stopping the operation until the court could consider a legal challenge brought by environmental groups. The president also suggested that the incoming governor, Rob Sand (D), should decide whether the operation goes forward.

item.title: Trump administration adds Megaspeed, key firm in Nvidia scandal, to trade blacklist
item.description: Administration officials have said the move has been under discussion for months. But the timing was attention-grabbing, coming the same day that Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after a personal intervention from President Donald Trump.

item.title: Deputy FBI director plans to retire after less than a year on the job, leading to a new shake-up at the bureau
item.description: Christopher Raia’s expected departure would create a vacancy in a critical position that is tasked with running the day-to-day operations of the FBI.

item.title: Nvidia shares close up more than 31% after Huang’s return, as markets reverse course following last week’s big losses
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index finished up 6.5 percent, and the S&P 500 rose 4.7 percent.

item.title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez, a California Democrat, to resign next month after sexual misconduct findings
item.description: The House Ethics Committee concluded that a House staffer was “sufficiently credible in her assertions that his conduct toward her was unwelcome” and constituted a violation of House rules and possibly criminal law. Gomez lost his reelection bid last month.

item.title: Trump orders military to halt plan to detonate stockpile of hazardous chemicals in Iowa
item.description: In a post on Truth Social, the president said the military can’t proceed without the approval of an appeals court and Iowa’s Democratic governor-elect, Rob Sand.

item.title: Trump plans to use Justice Department speech for political attack against California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a potential 2028 contender
item.description: The White House also released a slickly edited 85-second video criticizing Newsom’s effort to commute all state death sentences.

item.title: The best and wildest costumes from the Miss Universe pageant
item.description: Each year, delegates from around the world are tasked with presenting a costume that showcases something about their culture — often that includes flowers, animals, ethnic attire or symbols of national pride. And sometimes the result is high camp.
